question: Does my insurance change after my visa switches from D-4 to D-2?
required_facts: While taking language courses (D-4), insurance questions go to the language school
After the change to D-2 degree status the university insurance applies: at ERICA a KRW 25,000 group-insurance premium per semester, charged on the tuition bill
At Seoul, enrolled students' private-insurance premiums are paid by the university
National Health Insurance applies to international students at 50% of an alien resident's monthly premium

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul private-insurance rule; gold student is at ERICA

reference_answer: Yes. As a language-course (D-4) student you ask your language school about insurance; once you are a D-2 degree student at ERICA you are in the university group insurance (KRW 25,000 per semester, charged on your tuition bill), and National Health Insurance applies at 50% of an alien resident's monthly premium. (At the Seoul campus the university pays enrolled students' private-insurance premium instead.)
notes: Campus unstated and the university-insurance rule differs (ERICA KRW 25,000 on the tuition bill vs Seoul paid by the university) -> campus is a 2-branch attribute (8.3, 9.3). The language-school sentence exists only on the ERICA page (10.4.1). No page says whether NHI enrolment changes at the moment of the visa change, so that is not a required fact.

notes: Clarify question: 'Which visa do you hold?' question: Will immigration definitely approve my D-4 to D-2 change?
required_facts: No page guarantees approval; the decision is the immigration office's (not stated in the snapshot)
The D-4 to D-2 change needs, among others, the admission letter, tuition payment receipt, language-school attendance/completion certificate and transcript; fee KRW 130,000
With language-school attendance below 70%, a bank balance of KRW 20 million (KRW 10 million if the language school belongs to the university) and a statement are needed
reference_answer: No official page can promise approval; the immigration office decides. What the pages do give are the requirements: the admission letter, tuition payment receipt, language-school attendance certificate and transcript and the other listed documents, a KRW 130,000 fee, and, if your language-school attendance was below 70%, a bank balance of KRW 20 million (KRW 10 million for the university's own language school). Ask the ERICA OIA or the immigration office about your case.
notes: 10.3.1: requirements supported, the guarantee is not -> partial, abstain (9.1). Attendance rate is outside the vocabulary -> caveat, not a branch. Campus unstated but the rule is national.

question: Can I still get a part-time permit?
required_facts: Yes: D-2-8 visiting/exchange students can get a part-time work permit once 6 months have passed since entry
As an English-track student, TOEFL iBT 71 / IELTS 5.5 (or equivalent) meets the language requirement instead of TOPIK
Without meeting the language requirement, a year 3-4 undergraduate is limited to 10 hours per week
Caveat: previous-semester GPA of at least C (2.0)
reference_answer: Yes, once 6 months have passed since your entry on the D-2-8 visa. As an English-track student you can meet the language requirement with TOEFL iBT 71 or IELTS 5.5 (or equivalent) instead of TOPIK; without it, a third-year undergraduate is limited to 10 hours a week. Your previous-semester GPA must be at least 2.0, and you need the permit before you start working.
notes: All vocabulary attributes stated; time since entry and English score are outside the vocabulary -> caveats. condition_sets: Seoul checklist says 'Korean or English'; year 3 needs TOPIK 4. Campus unstated but the rule is national; the Seoul form/ERICA table hour conflict (10.4.4) does not affect the 10-hour figure for undergraduates without the language standard (both say 10).

reference_answer: The official pages do not say when to start the D-2 to D-10 change, so ask the ERICA OIA or the immigration office. They do say that with a Korean doctorate earned within the past 3 years and TOPIK 4 or higher you are exempt from the D-10-1 points system; you need a job search plan, proof of residence and the KRW 130,000 fee, and D-10-1 is granted up to 2 years, 6 months at a time.
